title: AI + Security & Safety — Don Bosco Durai
talk_summary: A security-focused talk arguing that agent frameworks running everything in one process with shared super-admin credentials create zero-trust problems, and proposing three layers: pre-production security/safety evals producing a risk score, enforcement via identity propagation and authorization, and observability with thresholds and anomaly detection. It is mostly conceptual governance framing rather than measured engineering results.

takeaways.technique: Per-tool credential isolation instead of shared process credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agent frameworks run agent/task/tools in one process, so tools share service-user super-admin credentials and any tool or third-party library can reach other credentials and prompts; recommends isolating so each tool only holds what it needs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one tool can technically access some other credentials which is in the same process

takeaways.technique: Identity propagation to the last data-access point
takeaways.what_they_do: Requires the requesting user's identity to be carried through agent -> task -> tool and enforced at the actual API/DB call, not just at entry, so agents acting on behalf of a user cannot exceed that user's permissions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to make sure the user identity is propagated across everywhere

takeaways.what_they_do: Proposes evals beyond response quality: prompt-injection tests, data-leakage tests, unauthorized-action tests, and runaway-loop tests, aggregated into a risk score that gates production promotion (including third-party agents).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you also need to have evales which are more security and safety focused

takeaways.technique: Dedicated approval agent with thresholds and human escalation
takeaways.what_they_do: Suggests a separate agent whose only job is checking approvals/results, with automatic approval up to a threshold and human-in-the-loop above it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could have another agent which all it does is just looks for approvals

takeaways.technique: Threshold-based failure-rate alerting on agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Says per-request monitoring is infeasible at scale, so define failure-rate thresholds and metrics and alert when exceeded, plus anomaly detection on agent behavior versus accepted boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it goes above that you can automatically create alert and look into it

takeaways.technique: Sandboxed execution as an enforcement layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames sandboxing as part of 'proactive enforcement' alongside guardrails, so agents run in an isolated environment rather than with ambient access to backend systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make sure you have the right guard rails you have the right enforcement you have the right sandbox
